findings.title: Computed schema keys discard the token expiry and refresh token
findings.body: Calling toString() on a Zod schema produces a literal property name (normally "[object Object]"), not a wildcard key. Both computed keys collide, and z.object strips unrecognized properties by default. Consequently, a sync response containing access_token, expires_in and refresh_token loses the latter two fields. Zoom then calculates a NaN expiry, and Office 365 cannot retain the refreshed expiry. Define explicit response fields and appropriate passthrough/normalization instead.

findings.title: Persist the parsed credentials rather than the safeParse result
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a safeParse envelope shaped as { success: true, data: ... }, whereas the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse call returned the credentials themselves. Saving this envelope as credential.key removes access_token and the other credential fields from the top level. This affects ordinary Google refreshes even with syncing disabled; subsequent service construction cannot parse the saved credential. Persist the result's data field.

findings.title: Normalize sync responses for SDK and Axios callers
findings.body: The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response, but several callers expect the return type of their original refresh function. Google Calendar, Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read response.data, and HubSpot reads accessToken and expiresIn directly. A fetch Response has none of these properties, regardless of the JSON returned by the endpoint, so enabling syncing breaks their refresh paths. Parse and adapt the sync response to a consistent contract and update these callers.

findings.title: Do not replace an omitted refresh token with a placeholder
findings.body: The helper unconditionally injects the literal "refresh_token" when a response omits a refresh token, including when credential sharing is disabled. Office 365 explicitly allows the provider to omit refresh_token and merges the parsed response into the existing credentials. This change overwrites the existing usable refresh token with the placeholder, causing the next refresh to fail. Preserve the existing token when no replacement is returned.

findings.title: Import Prisma before using it in Salesforce initialization
findings.body: The new initialization path calls prisma.credential.update, but this file does not import or declare prisma. This causes a TypeScript error and, if transpiled without type checking, a ReferenceError after a successful token refresh, preventing Salesforce client initialization.

findings.title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
findings.body: The added Salesforce refresh always posts directly to Salesforce using credentialKey.refresh_token; it never uses refreshOAuthTokens or checks whether credential sharing is enabled. Synced credentials whose refresh tokens are managed exclusively by the parent application therefore cannot initialize the Salesforce integration. Use the configured refresh source, and initialize the jsforce connection with the newly returned access token rather than the old credentialKey.access_token.

findings.title: Pass the credential owner's user ID to the sync request
findings.body: The third argument of refreshOAuthTokens is a Cal.com user ID and is sent as calcomUserId, but this call passes the credential row ID. These IDs are unrelated, so the parent application will look up the wrong user or fail to find one. Once response handling is corrected, this can also save another user's token onto this credential. Carry credential.userId into refreshAccessToken and pass it here.

findings.title: Send Zoom's app slug rather than its integration directory name
findings.body: This call sends appSlug="zoomvideo" to the parent endpoint, while Zoom credentials and the app store use appId/slug="zoom" (as shown in the Zoom callback). A parent application mapping refresh requests by the same appSlug used for credential synchronization cannot resolve this request. Pass "zoom" here.

findings.title: Clear credential invalidation when replacing credentials
findings.body: Updating an existing credential only replaces key and leaves invalid unchanged. Google and Zoom, among others, mark credentials invalid after an unrecoverable authentication failure. If the parent application reconnects the account and sends fresh credentials through this webhook, the endpoint reports success but the credential remains invalid and unavailable for normal use. Reset invalid when accepting a valid replacement credential.
